passage:
Lakshmi: You look stressed. Short again this month?

Jyoti: Third month running. I don't get it. My salary isn't small.

Lakshmi: Do you know where it goes?

Jyoti: Not exactly. So I'm going to write down every payment I make from my phone, for one month. Everything.

(A month later, at the pantry.)

Jyoti: Look at this. Food delivery is the biggest item. More than transport and phone put together.

Lakshmi: Seriously? I would have guessed rent.

Jyoti: Rent is fixed. This is the leak. So now there's a weekly cap on delivery, and cooking twice.

Lakshmi: Easier than a guessed budget.

Jyoti: Yes. Numbers I can see are better than promises I make to myself.

qa.q: Which item was the biggest in Jyoti's month of records?
qa.a: Food delivery was the biggest item, more than transport and phone put together.

qa.q: What was Jyoti feeling when saying that the salary is not small?
qa.a: Jyoti felt puzzled and stressed at being short for the third month in a row.

qa.q: What could Jyoti try if the weekly cap keeps being broken, and why?
qa.a: Jyoti could cook more meals in advance so the cap is easy to keep, since the cap works only when an alternative exists.

qa.q: How might Lakshmi see the results compared with the earlier guess about rent?
qa.a: Lakshmi was surprised, because rent had been the guess, which shows how easily a guessed budget can miss the real leak.

grounding: After running short an employee records every payment for a month, finds the biggest leak and sets a weekly cap on it.

passage:
I'm Trisha, and in March I ran out of money four days before salary for the second month in a row. I'd guessed a budget in January, a neat one, and it clearly wasn't real.
So in April I did something boring. Every time I paid on my phone, I wrote it in a notes file that evening: amount, what, why. My flatmate Sarika laughed at me the first week.
By the end of the month the list was three pages long. I sorted it into groups on a Sunday. Rent, fine. Travel, fine. Food delivery: ₹7,400. More than my travel and phone bill together. Most of it after 10 p.m., when I was too tired to cook.
So now there's a cap, ₹1,200 a week for delivery, and Sarika and I cook double on Sundays. In May I reached salary day with ₹2,000 left.

qa.q: How much did Trisha spend on food delivery in April?
How did Trisha feel on seeing the food delivery total?
qa.a: Trisha was likely shocked and a little embarrassed, since it beat travel and phone together, but relieved to finally see the leak.

qa.q: If you were Trisha, what would you check next?
qa.a: Keep tracking for another month with the cap, to see whether the Sunday cooking really holds the late-night orders down.

qa.q: What is it like for Sarika to watch this?
qa.a: Sarika laughs at the note-taking at first, but ends up part of the fix, cooking double with Trisha on Sundays.

grounding: Shows an employee logging every phone payment for a month, finding food delivery the largest leak and setting a weekly cap.

Buddy-programme note, week 12. Akash, team lead, for HR records.
In week 6 Kalyani asked me for an advance on her salary; it was her second request. I didn't approve it, but I offered to help her look at where the money went. She agreed to log every phone payment for one month in a small notebook and show me.
Today she brought it. She had grouped the entries herself. The largest line wasn't rent or travel; it was food delivery, ₹6,800, almost all ordered to her desk during late shifts. She looked up and said, 'I thought my problem was the rent.'
She has now set herself ₹1,500 a week for delivery, and asked whether the canteen could stay open during late shifts. I have passed that request to facilities today. I will check in with her at week 16.

qa.q: How much did Kalyani spend on food delivery in the month?
What does Kalyani's line 'I thought my problem was the rent' suggest?
qa.a: She is surprised and a little embarrassed that her guess was wrong, but relieved to have real evidence to act on.

qa.q: What else could support Kalyani's weekly cap?
qa.a: Alongside the canteen request, bringing food from home on late-shift days, so the cap does not rest on willpower alone.

qa.q: How does the change look to Akash, who wrote the note?
qa.a: Akash sees Kalyani move from asking for advances to fixing the cause herself, and backs it by passing the canteen request to facilities.

grounding: Shows an employee who kept running short tracking a month of payments, spotting food delivery as the biggest leak and setting a weekly cap.
